structured_output.world_model: Time ≈ fixed ~0.1 s + steps × per-step cost; per-step cost is pixel-proportional compute plus a large memory-bound part on the 31×31 maps. Accuracy rises slowly with steps (~0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch). The tip (E036) is 5.31 s, with a population mean of ~0.752–0.753, so it sits at the accuracy cliff. Any non-systems change should be shaded about −0.1 pp, and the seeds 3–12 gate carries a winner's curse. Systems-only changes (I066) are the only safe ones, worth about 0.03–0.06 s. The early-resolution dial is mostly cheap, but the 20 px phase is already cheap per step, so I060 saves ≲0.1 s. Freeze dose (I062, I063) has a nonlinear cliff, as E037 showed. A BN recalibration (I064) is a plausible accuracy gain that costs a small amount of time.

forecasts.reason: Moving 23 steps from 24 px to 20 px saves ~0.06 s; the accuracy cost is within noise but likely slightly negative, below the keep gate.
Removing 12 steps costs ~0.1–0.15 pp at a population mean already at the cliff; the held-out gate of 0.7545 is unlikely to be met.
Partial freeze of conv1 at 60% saves some 31×31 traffic, but E037 suggests an early freeze costs accuracy.
Moving the freeze 5% earlier saves ~0.04 s; the accuracy change is small and probably slightly negative.
BN recalibration may help a little (+0.1 pp) at a cost of ~0.04 s; the BN stats from Lookahead are likely already adequate.
16 px is a very coarse start; the saving is small (~0.04 s), and 1×1 final maps risk an accuracy loss.
A math-identical warm-up trims trial 0's prepare overhead by ~0.02–0.03 s on the mean; accuracy is bit-identical.

cruxes: What is the true population mean accuracy of the tip: 0.752 or 0.754? It decides whether any trim is feasible at all.
Does the accuracy cliff in E037 come from freezing before the 28→32 px switch, or from the freeze dose itself?
How much of the remaining time is fixed overhead (prepare, first-call costs) versus per-step cost?
